top.title: Brandon Aiyuk returns to 49ers facility, speaks to media in Santa Clara
top.description: San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk warms up before an NFL game against the Arizona Cardinals in Santa Clara, Calif., Sunday, Oct. 6, 2024. (Jed Jacobsohn/AP) Disgruntled San Francisco 49ers star wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk is back in Santa Clara, turning an otherwise standard Friday practice day for the team into a surreal scene. Ahead of a scheduled 3 p.m. meeting, the wide receiver appeared at the team's business offices, which are about a tenth of a mile west of Levi's Stadium and half a mile from the team's practice facility. Aiyuk arrived in a black van along with his new agent, Drew Rosenhaus, with both giving brief statements to the throng of reporters stationed in front of the office. Drew Rosenhaus and Brandon Aiyuk stop and briefly address the media before his meeting with #49ers, which is about to begin. https://t.co/A3ClTXIce1 - Nick Wagoner (@nwagoner) November 6, 2026 "Obviously, Brandon is here to meet with the team. Fortunately, he's feeling good physically; he's healthy, he's ready to get back to work," Rosenhaus said. "Don't really have any comment about where he's going to play. We'll keep that between us and the Niners. But obviously, we're here with all the right intentions." With a news helicopter circling above the gathering, Aiyuk told reporters it was "nice to see y'all" before he said: "I'm feeling great, feeling healthy. A long recovery process, long rehab process, but I'm back to 100% and looking to get reinstated into the National Football League." As Aiyuk and Rosenhaus began to walk into the 49ers offices, the former two-time 1,000-yard receiver repeated his last line to a reporter who shouted a question at him. Rosenhaus declined most other inquiries, saying they may have a few more comments after the meeting, but when California Post reporter Evan Webeck asked about Aiyuk's outstanding arrest warrant, Rosenhaus looked back over his shoulder and said, "We're working on that." Throughout Friday, Santa Clara police cars were spotted around the 49ers team facilities, something team beat reporters noted was uncommon for a practice day. The department put out a warrant for Aiyuk's arrest in June , stemming from Aiyuk posting a video of himself driving up to 104 mph on city streets last December. Aiyuk is appearing at the 49ers facility as part of his attempt to return to the NFL. He's expected to have to negotiate with the 49ers over a reported $13 million that the NFL says he owes the team, money stemming from the signing bonus he got when he signed a four-year, $120 million extension in 2024. Aiyuk hasn't played a game in more than two years since going down with a knee injury in October 2024 and has been on the reserve/left squad list after leaving the Niners late last season. He fired agent Ryan Williams during his long-running dispute with the 49ers and was without representation until he recently hired Rosenhaus. top.title: Green Bay Packers guard reveals how he’s adjusting to new role in the offensive line
top.description: The Green Bay Packers made an unexpected lineup decision in Week 8, assigning Laken Tomlinson to right guard despite the veteran having started at that position just once during his 12-year NFL career. Tomlinson said he is adjusting well to the new position, although the switch proved more challenging last week because of the condensed schedule and limited practice opportunities. “I mean, it’s definitely a challenge, especially last week,” Tomlinson shared. Green Bay’s Thursday night game in Week 8 left little room for a proper practice session, forcing Tomlinson to adjust to right guard with limited work alongside his teammates. This week’s longer preparation window, however, gives him more time to get comfortable on the right side of the offensive line. Laken Tomlinson with the Green Bay Packers Dec 8, 2024; Glendale, Arizona, USA; Seattle Seahawks guard Laken Tomlinson (70) against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images “This week, especially going into the long weekend, I had some extra time to kind of just like go over some stuff on my own. Work on my technique and just work on flipping things technique-wise, and having these two days of practice. So definitely a lot more comfortable now,” the Packers veteran remarked. Tomlinson has logged 11,131 career snaps at left guard, compared with just 131 at right guard following his Week 8 start. Despite his limited experience on the opposite side, the Packers’ coaching staff felt his performance was too strong to take him out of the lineup. Mandatory Credit: Samantha Madar/Green Bay Press Gazette -USA TODAY NETWORK With starting left guard Aaron Banks back in the lineup, Green Bay had no room to keep Tomlinson on that side of the offensive line. top.title: Mutfwang: Educated Nigerians masterminding corruption, institutional decay
top.description: …says professionals behind major governance failures …challenges graduates to choose integrity over wealth By Joseph Erunke, Abuja Plateau State Governor, Caleb Mutfwang, has accused educated Nigerians of masterminding some of the country’s most damaging corruption scandals, financial fraud and institutional abuses, saying the nation’s governance crisis is not a result of a shortage of intellectual capacity but a failure of conscience. Mutfwang said some of the most sophisticated acts of financial fraud, contract manipulation, money laundering and subversion of public institutions were perpetrated by people whose academic qualifications and professional expertise should ordinarily be deployed for national development. The governor spoke on Friday in Abuja while delivering the convocation lecture at the 15th Convocation Ceremony of Veritas University. In his lecture titled, “Building the Nigeria We Want: The Role of the Educated Mind,” he warned that education without moral discipline had become a dangerous instrument against the country’s progress. He challenged the graduating students to rethink the purpose of university education, insisting that academic certificates and intellectual brilliance would amount to little if deployed for selfish interests at the expense of society. According to him, Nigeria’s development challenges cannot be blamed entirely on inadequate manpower or lack of expertise, as many individuals responsible for undermining public institutions are highly educated and professionally trained. Describing the situation as an uncomfortable reality the country must confront, Mutfwang said some of Nigeria’s most entrenched governance failures were products of educated minds. He said: “Indeed, I make an uncomfortable observation: the afflictions I diagnosed earlier, prebendalism, the privatisation of public office, grand corruption, the capture of institutions, are almost never the work of illiterate minds. They are overwhelmingly executed by educated minds. “The contract, the doctored account, the laundered fund, the ingenious evasion of law. All these are the signatures of trained minds. This is the paradox we must confront. The educated mind is at once our greatest hope, and when corrupted, it becomes our most sophisticated danger.” The governor also cited internet fraudsters, popularly known as Yahoo boys, as an example of intelligence deployed in the wrong direction, arguing that criminal ingenuity reflected a lack of moral restraint rather than an absence of intelligence. “The Yahoo boy is certainly not a derelict. He is a work of intelligence, but intelligence wrongly applied,” he said. Mutfwang maintained that Nigeria had no shortage of brilliant citizens, noting the achievements of Nigerians across different professions and on international platforms. It is too early to say whether the New Jersey Devils ’ decision to acquire goaltender Connor Hellebuyck will be a success, but the early returns on the deal represent a win for both the team and the goaltender. Hellebuyck was in net Thursday night for New Jersey’s 5-4 victory over the St. Louis Blues in overtime. Hellebuyck has improved his has a 4-0 record in his first four games in a New Jersey uniform and he has allowed 10 goals. He has a 2.44 goals against average with an .891 save percentage. The four-time NHL All-Star famously backstopped the U.S. Olympic hockey team to the gold medal in the 2026 Winter Olympics. top.description: Head coach Casey Alexander of the Kansas State Wildcats point down court in the second half against the South Dakota State Jackrabbits at Bramlage Coliseum on November 3, 2026 in Manhattan, Kansas. (Photo by Peter G. Aiken/Getty Images) | Peter G. Aiken/Getty Images For the first time since the start of the Tom Asbury era, the new coach at K-State lost the first game of his tenure. Not exactly a good omen start for the Casey Alexander era. But the show must go on, and the second game of the season is on deck for the Kansas State Wildcats. Cal-State Northridge (CSUN) is in town tonight to take on the new-look Wildcats. It’s been 39 years since the last time the Cats and Matadors have met on the hardwood, and the two squads enter tonight at 0-1 on the young season. Despite a great first game from Pape N’Diaye (Pop En-jy), with the Xavier transfer notching 18 points and 8 rebounds to lead the team in both categories, the Wildcats struggled on defense all evening, falling to South Dakota State 68-66 on Tuesday night in Bramlage. It was the same kind of lapses that cost the Cats in exhibition games versus Missouri and Nebraska, and yet in all three games the Wildcats fought to the end and made it close before ultimately falling. But moral victories don’t count on the Win/Loss sheet, and Casey Alexander has yet to win a game, officially or unofficially, as the head coach at Kansas State. It’s time for Casey to step up to the plate and actually knock one out of the park. K-State needs to win and get back on schedule for this season. top.title: 2027: APGA adopts Tinubu, flags off nationwide campaign
top.description: …Soludo cites South-East projects, urges strategic voting By Steve Oko The All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) has adopted President Bola Tinubu as its presidential candidate for the 2027 general election, with Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, saying the decision was informed by the need for progressive forces to work together. Soludo made the declaration on Friday while flagging off APGA’s nationwide election campaign at Alex Ekwueme Square, Awka, Anambra State, where the party unveiled more than 253 candidates contesting various elective positions across the country. The governor, who is APGA’s National Leader, said the decision to support Tinubu was consistent with the party’s political tradition, recalling that APGA had similarly adopted former President Goodluck Jonathan in the 2011 and 2015 presidential elections. He said the party’s support for Tinubu was also informed by what he described as the Federal Government’s commitment to the South-East, particularly in infrastructure development. “Today, as we unveil our campaign as the foremost progressive party in Nigeria, we are also officially adopting President Bola Tinubu as the presidential candidate of APGA. “We did it in 2011 and 2015 for President Jonathan. We are repeating it in 2027 because progressives are working together to support a President who loves Ndi Igbo and Ndi Anambra,” Soludo declared. Citing the dualisation and rehabilitation of the Enugu-Onitsha Expressway and other federal projects in the region, the governor urged voters to approach the 2027 elections with political pragmatism rather than sentiment. He said voting decisions should be guided by tangible benefits, enlightened self-interest and strategic political considerations capable of advancing the interests of the South-East. Soludo also charged APGA candidates and members to intensify grassroots mobilisation through door-to-door campaigns, assuring them that he would personally join the candidates in soliciting votes. He expressed confidence in the party’s electoral prospects, urging voters to distinguish between reason and emotion ahead of the January 16 and February 6, 2027 elections. At the event, Soludo presented party flags to 44 APGA candidates contesting legislative seats in Anambra State. The candidates comprised three senatorial candidates, 11 House of Representatives candidates and 30 State House of Assembly candidates. Earlier, APGA National Chairman, Barrister Sly Ezeokenwa, commended Soludo for what he described as transparent and competitive party primaries conducted in compliance with electoral laws. Ezeokenwa attributed the influx of new members into the party to Soludo’s people-oriented policies, describing Anambra as APGA’s political stronghold. He expressed confidence that the party would record a decisive victory in the forthcoming elections. top.title: SCOUTING VALENCIA: Should be a breeze in theory, but Valencia at the Mestalla is never easy
top.description: Mexican coach Javier Aguirre is presented as the new manager of Valencia CF at a press conference at the Mestalla stadium in Valencia, on September 28, 2026. (Photo by Jose Miguel Fernandez/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images Valencia are on their third coach after just 11 league matches. Carlos Corberán’s dismissal, Óscar Sánchez’s brief spell in charge and Javier Aguirre’s arrival have brought two wins, three draws and six defeats. They have scored eight goals and conceded 17. The lack of goals is their most immediate problem. Valencia have created 10.8 non-penalty expected goals, ranking 17th in La Liga, but scored only six when penalties and own goals are excluded. They are struggling both to create enough and to finish the chances they do get. Umar Sadiq leads the squad with 1.8 npxG and two goals. Hugo Duro and Arnaut Danjuma have yet to score despite chances worth 1.6 and 1.4 npxG respectively. Valencia’s most productive attacking spell came in their seventh and eighth matches, when they averaged 1.85 npxG. They have conceded 14.8 npxG, an average of 1.34 per match, with 14 non-penalty goals allowed. Opponents are scoring roughly in line with the chances Valencia concede. Much of their defending takes place close to home. Their defensive actions occur an average of 30 metres from their own goal line, the deepest figure in La Liga. Their PPDA of 15.8 is also the league’s highest, indicating that opponents are allowed more passes before Valencia intervene outside their own defensive third. The league average is 12.4. That limited pressure is reflected in where matches are played. Valencia account for just 36.4% of final-third passes, the lowest share in the division, and have held the larger share in only two of their 11 games. Across the pitch’s 24 zones, they have controlled five, compared with 11 for their opponents. Possession has offered little relief. Valencia complete 313 open-play passes per match, ranking 15th, and only 21.2% of the passes they receive arrive in the final third. Their passing has generated 9.3 expected threat, the second-lowest total in La Liga. Danjuma leads that measure with 0.97 xT, followed by Pepelu on 0.93 and Luis Rioja on 0.71. Their most-used formation has been 4-4-2, while José Gayà and Justin de Haas are their most frequent passing partnership, exchanging 23 passes. Valencia average 10.3 non-penalty shots per match, each worth 0.10 npxG. Their average shooting distance of 17.8 metres ranks ninth shortest, but the goals have not followed. They have spent almost 64% of their season level and just 10.1% ahead. Aguirre’s task is to give them more ways to move up the pitch and turn those long periods at parity into winning positions. So far, Valencia have spent too much time defending and made too little of their opportunities when they arrive.

top.title: Carson Hocevar Finally Feels NASCAR’s Heat
top.description: HOMESTEAD, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 06: NASCAR Cup Series driver, Carson Hocevar speaks to the media during a press conference at Homestead-Miami Speedway on November 06, 2026 in Homestead, Florida. (Photo by Jared C. Tilton/Getty Images) Getty Images There was probably nowhere else Carson Hocevar wanted to be less than the third floor of the media center at Homestead-Miami Speedway on Friday. Of course, Hocevar didn’t really need to be at the site of the final NASCAR Cup Series race of the 2026 season. That’s because he won’t be racing on Sunday. His team, Spire Motorsports, announced earlier in the week that it was suspending the driver of the No. 77 Chevrolet for the season finale. So no one expected Hocevar to be at Homestead-Miami Speedway on Friday. Yet there he was. And judging by his demeanor, there were probably a dozen other places he’d rather have been. It all started the previous Sunday at Martinsville Speedway. During the race, Hocevar, apparently angered by something, brake-checked Team Penske driver Austin Cindric not once, but twice. The result was considerable damage to Cindric’s Ford, forcing him to retire from the event. Shortly after Spire announced its suspension, NASCAR handed Hocevar another helping of consequences, fining him $100,000 and docking him 25 driver points. It was the latest chapter in a season filled with on-track incidents that left crashed cars and angry drivers in their wake. On Thursday, Hocevar released a video on his YouTube channe l. In it, he took responsibility for the actions that put him on the sidelines this weekend. He admitted he was the “bad guy” and appeared genuinely remorseful. FORBES | By Greg Engle Carson Hocevar’s NASCAR Season Ends With A Lesson In Accountability Apparently, taking responsibility for your actions is considerably easier when you’re doing it from the comfort of your own YouTube channel. Friday, when meeting with the media, Hocevar looked like a driver who would much rather have been anywhere else than answering questions about the mess he’d made. But he showed up, and he didn’t shy away from acknowledging that he knew his actions at Martinsville could bring serious consequences. “Probably, you know, before I started hitting the brakes,” Hocevar said when asked when he realized he might face significant punishment. “I knew it was like a possibility for sure. But, you know, I took a percentage risk of that.” In other words, he knew there was a chance the stunt would cost him. He just apparently wasn’t expecting the bill to be quite so large. top.title: Jazz owner Ryan Smith stands firmly behind Will Hardy and front office amid disappointing start
top.description: From left, Austin Ainge, president of basketball operations for the Utah Jazz, Will Hardy, head coach of the Utah Jazz, and Ryan Smith, owner of the Utah Jazz, look on during a Salt Lake City Summer League game between the Utah Jazz and Atlanta Hawks at the Huntsman Center in Salt Lake City on Saturday, July 4, 2026. | Rio Giancarlo, Deseret News Ryan Smith understands why fans are frustrated with the Utah Jazz’s 1-7 start. He’s watching the same games they are. But despite the early season struggles, the team’s owner isn’t interested in making any drastic changes. Appearing Friday on KSL’s “Scotty G. & The Coach” podcast , the 48-year-old Smith addressed the Jazz’s difficult start , the development of the team’s young players and the expectations surrounding a roster that entered the season with plenty of excitement . His message was clear: He has 100% confidence in the people leading the organization, notably head coach Will Hardy and president of basketball operations Austin Ainge. “Will’s our guy. Austin’s our guy. Like we’re not changing anything,” Smith said. “Like we’re going to go through this, we’re going to work together. We got Danny (Ainge), and like I love our group.” Smith acknowledged, though, that the young team’s current performance hasn’t met expectations, particularly after the moves the team made that brought significant excitement to the Salt Lake Valley. The Jazz got a defensive anchor in Jaren Jackson Jr., added another highly touted prospect in rookie Darryn Peterson and entered the season hoping to take a meaningful step forward. Bad luck to start But injuries and inconsistent play have made that transition difficult. “No one’s ducking where we’re at,” Smith said. “We’re going to have to go through it, but if I look at our season so far, like there’s been really, really bright spots.” Smith pointed to Utah’s explosive 47-point first quarter against the Los Angeles Lakers at the Delta Center on Oct. 25 as an example of what the team can look like when everything clicks. top.description: CHAPEL HILL, NC - SEPTEMBER 23: An Atlantic Coast Conference field hockey logoed pylon before a game between Wake Forest and North Carolina at Karen Shelton Stadium on September 23, 2022 in Chapel Hill, North Carolina. (Photo by Andy Mead/ISI Photos/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Syracuse Orange got their 1st ACC Championship of the 26-27 athletic year when the field hockey squad defeated Boston College in penalty strokes. It’s the first ACC Championship for the Orange program, which will now wait to find out who they will play in the NCAA Championship. The Orange and Eagles were scoreless through four quarters and the overtime period, so the title was decided by a penalty stroke shootout. Field hockey shootouts are a bit different as players get 8 seconds to try and score. The possession doesn’t end until the clock expires, or the offensive player loses possession. It’s a situation where patience is critical and the offensive player tries to make the goalies move laterally to open up shooting space. Syracuse goalie Jesse Eiselin denied the first BC attempt and Syracuse’s Sammie Goin was able to convert. Eiselin made another save in the 2nd round and Taylor Bigbie converted to put the Orange up two. Eiselin stopped the 3rd and 4th Eagles’ shooters and clinched Syracuse’s automatic bid. After beating Louisville in the opening round, Syracuse ended North Carolina’s quest for a 10th straight title with a shootout win in the semifinal. It was Tane King in goal for that win, so both Orange goalies were clutch under pressure. Bo Madden was selected as the Tournament MVP with her sister Hattie, Aubrey Turner and Eiselin also earning All-Tournament Team honors. The Orange will learn their NCAA opponent this Sunday night.

top.description: Mandatory Credit: Kelley L Cox-Imagn Images The situation with Kristaps Porzingis has somewhat derailed the Warriors’ season , but they aren’t about to give up. With Stephen Curry on the team, they still have every incentive to win now, and Yaxel Lendrborg’s rise to power has given them renewed hope of a competitive season. Of course, that’s not to mention Jimmy Butler’s impending return. After tearing his ACL last season, Butler has been in full recovery, but there’s good reason to believe that we can expect him back before the deadline. According to the latest reports, he’s ahead in the process, adding additional optimism that he can help the Warriors make a push this season. “The same can be said regarding Jimmy Butler, with the Warriors continuing to signal that they aren’t thinking about trading. ACL tears require a lengthy recovery time, ranging from 9 to 12 months. While modern medical advances have made it easier than ever for players to regain their strength, it’s still a difficult process that can alter careers. Over the past year, Butler has experienced this for himself, and it has shifted his entire perspective on the last act of his basketball story. Butler, 37, signed with the Warriors in the summer of 2025, hoping to usher in a new era of prosperity for the franchise. The struggles sparked endless trade rumors, with Butler himself at the center of most of them. The longtime veteran is on a $56 million expiring contract, giving him unique value on the trade market. One suggested deal involved the Warriors trading Butler in exchange for Franz Wagner . Such an arrangement was always unlikely, however, as the Warriors are against trading Jimmy. Mutfwang said some of the most sophisticated acts of financial fraud, contract manipulation, money laundering and subversion of public institutions were perpetrated by people whose academic qualifications and professional expertise should ordinarily be deployed for national development. nigeria.description: …Soludo cites South-East projects, urges strategic voting By Steve Oko The All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) has adopted President Bola Tinubu as its presidential candidate for the 2027 general election, with Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, saying the decision was informed by the need for progressive forces to work together. Soludo made the declaration on Friday while flagging off APGA’s nationwide election campaign at Alex Ekwueme Square, Awka, Anambra State, where the party unveiled more than 253 candidates contesting various elective positions across the country. The governor, who is APGA’s National Leader, said the decision to support Tinubu was consistent with the party’s political tradition, recalling that APGA had similarly adopted former President Goodluck Jonathan in the 2011 and 2015 presidential elections. He said the party’s support for Tinubu was also informed by what he described as the Federal Government’s commitment to the South-East, particularly in infrastructure development. “Today, as we unveil our campaign as the foremost progressive party in Nigeria, we are also officially adopting President Bola Tinubu as the presidential candidate of APGA. “We did it in 2011 and 2015 for President Jonathan. We are repeating it in 2027 because progressives are working together to support a President who loves Ndi Igbo and Ndi Anambra,” Soludo declared. Citing the dualisation and rehabilitation of the Enugu-Onitsha Expressway and other federal projects in the region, the governor urged voters to approach the 2027 elections with political pragmatism rather than sentiment. He said voting decisions should be guided by tangible benefits, enlightened self-interest and strategic political considerations capable of advancing the interests of the South-East. Soludo also charged APGA candidates and members to intensify grassroots mobilisation through door-to-door campaigns, assuring them that he would personally join the candidates in soliciting votes. He expressed confidence in the party’s electoral prospects, urging voters to distinguish between reason and emotion ahead of the January 16 and February 6, 2027 elections. nigeria.title: US reports highest number of measles cases in 35 years
nigeria.description: The United States has recorded more than 5,000 cases of measles this year, the highest number in 35 years, according to an official count released Friday. So far in 2026, 5,182 confirmed cases of the highly contagious but highly preventable disease have been reported across the country, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), the nation’s leading public health agency. That compares with 2,289 cases during all of 2025, and is the highest level recorded by the CDC since 1991. State health officials have reported at least eight measles-related deaths, including among very young children. Pediatrician Adam Ratner, who specializes in infectious disease, told AFP such deaths are “tragic, and that is completely preventable.” Measles was declared eradicated from the United States in 2000 thanks to vaccination, but in recent years it has made a strong comeback, fueled by declining vaccination rates and growing public distrust of health authorities. President Donald Trump’s Health Secretary Robert Kennedy Jr. is accused of fanning that distrust. He is known for his vaccine skepticism and has repeatedly disseminated misinformation about the measles vaccine and downplayed the dangers of the disease. “Robert F. Kennedy Jr. does not believe that measles is a big problem and and does not want to believe that there are deaths from measles,” Ratner said. “The burden of these diseases will fall on children, who are not the ones who are making these decisions.” Measles causes fever, respiratory symptoms and a rash, and in some cases more serious complications such as pneumonia and brain inflammation, which can lead to severe long-term health problems or even death. Before the vaccine was developed in the early 1960s, measles killed hundreds of children each year across the US. It continues to claim tens of thousands of lives worldwide. The ADC says it will appeal. Obi, the Nigeria Democratic Congress presidential candidate, described the ruling as “unsettling and surprising”. The case now puts the spotlight on the judiciary’s role in resolving internal party disputes and on whether opposition parties can maintain stable platforms as the election approaches. The OK Movement accused them of fuelling divisions; the NDC campaign dismissed the dispute as a distraction, while the Obidient coordinator’s aide said he was focused on mobilising support for Obi. The public disagreements are a reminder that a broad support base needs clear roles and disciplined coordination to turn enthusiasm into effective political mobilisation. The task ahead For the Obidient Movement, the immediate challenge is to keep attention on voters, organisation and the issues facing Nigerians. The movement’s strength will be measured not only by the size of its support, but by how effectively it organises that support across communities and sustains a credible campaign. business.title: U.S. Treasury Cuts Off MEXC From U.S. Financial System Over Alleged $16 Billion in Illicit Flows
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine U.S. Treasury Cuts Off MEXC From U.S. Financial System Over Alleged $16 Billion in Illicit Flows The U.S. Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network issued a final order Friday that will cut offshore exchange MEXC Global off from the American banking system over alleged links to sanctions evasion by Iran, North Korea and Russia, the department said . FinCEN’s order, published as a PDF pending Federal Register placement, finds MEXC a “primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance” under section 9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act. Thirty days after that Register notice, covered U.S. financial institutions will be barred from any funds transfer — including convertible virtual currency — to or from MEXC. Reuters reported the same cut-off Friday afternoon. Treasury framed the move as part of Operation Economic Outcast. It is not an OFAC sanctions designation: the order says it does not rewrite Bank Secrecy Act duties or OFAC rules, and it is a FinCEN funds-transmittal ban rather than a Section 311 proposed rulemaking. Treasury alleges MEXC facilitated at least $16 billion in illicit flows from May 2021 through May 2026, including nearly $1.5 billion tied to Russian sanctions evasion and about $22 million linked to Iran’s Central Bank and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ Qods Force. The platform was still processing trades with sanctioned Garantex and successor Grinex as recently as June 2026, more than four years after OFAC designated Garantex, the release says. What the order does — and when The order , signed by FinCEN Deputy Director Jimmy L. Kirby, covers MEXC Global and named affiliates operating outside the United States, including Seychelles-incorporated MEXC Global Ltd / MX Global Ltd, Estonia’s MEXC Estonia OÜ, Switzerland’s GIDA Technology AG and the U.K.’s MXC Global Ltd, plus successors. Patrick Steven Yaroch, 37, of Ashburn, Virginia, entered pleas to wire fraud and money laundering in federal court in Alexandria. U.S. District Judge Patricia Tolliver Giles accepted the plea. He faces up to 20 years in prison and is scheduled for sentencing on March 4, 2027. Court papers put the illicit haul at $2,474,380.66. I moved from being a digital media professional writing stories, articles and shaping narratives to becoming an analyst in the energy sector, working across the oil and gas and renewable subsectors. The journey across these two industries that are worlds apart has taught me lessons on starting over You are never really starting from scratch No matter what you are starting over at or what you are getting into, it is important to realise that you are never truly starting from zero. Where ‘zero’ means the state of having nothing: skills, experience, network, intelligence, and others. While it may indeed appear that you do not have the things you consider as being critical to starting over, you actually have what you have: the knowledge, skills and experiences that have shaped your life and marked your journey up to this present moment, and this is invaluable. Also, having a strong knowledge of yourself is also an incredible resource when starting over, as it helps you to discern and differentiate challenges that are due to your personality, and challenges that are due to the circumstance of starting over. Your ‘Next Best Move’ is hidden within your network When we think of network, it is easy to limit it to close friends, relatives or even acquaintances. This is quite a restrictive and limiting view of the concept of network. Your network also includes ‘strangers’ and your internet community. In my case, I knew of the opportunity in the energy sector through a friend whom I had met on Instagram. It gets more interesting. By the time I was preparing for my first interview, I knew that I had zero knowledge about the current state of the sector. Thanks again to Instagram, I reached out to someone I followed who I knew worked in the sector, and she offered a free virtual coffee chat. I went into the interview more confident in what value I could offer and what mattered for such a role. Transferable skills are invaluable Prior to my career pivot, my only exposure to the energy sector aside from buying fuel and gas was a seminar paper I had written in my final year investigating annual shifts in fuel pump prices. At its centre is Itohan, played by Nancy Isime, a woman whose world is shaken by loss and by truths she never saw coming. What follows is a story about grief, the quiet kind that stays in a home long after the visitors have gone. It is about family, the people who hold us up and sometimes weigh us down. And it is about love that has to keep choosing to stay, even when it hurts. You will see yourself in it. In the person trying to hold everyone together. In the things left unsaid at the dinner table. In the slow, uneven way healing actually happens. A film that looks as good as it feels The cinematography deserves its own round of applause. Every frame feels deliberate, from the rich reds and golds of Edo tradition to the close, quiet moments where a single look says everything. The camera knows when to celebrate and when to simply sit with a character in her pain. This is a film made for the big screen. There is a reason it all feels so assured. Loving Itohan is from GREOH Studios , and Jade studio has never been afraid to go big, with daring, genre-bending stories like Gangs of Lagos. This time, GREOH goes deep instead, trading spectacle for the messy, tender feelings we all carry. True to form, it also hands the director’s chair to a fresh talent, Orobosa Ikponmwen , the latest in a line of new directors the studio has backed, from Kayode Kasum to Loukman Ali. And for Nancy Isime, this is her very first project as an executive producer. You can feel how much of herself she has poured into it, in front of the camera and behind it. Alongside her, Uzor Arukwe, Martha Ehinome Orhiere, Dorathy Bachor, Grace Dein Coker, Chioma Nwosu, Florence Sunday and newcomer Obehi Aburime bring the family to life. Don’t judge it by the trailer If the trailer has you thinking you know where this is going, trust us, you don’t. Go with someone you love. Bring tissues. And maybe call your mum afterwards. entertainment.title: Dayo Akinbode: What Travelling to Cuba Taught Me About Money
entertainment.description: I went to Cuba for the salsa, the cigars, the rum and those gorgeous vintage cars. I never imagined that, somewhere between admiring the colourful streets and enjoying the Caribbean sunshine, I would receive an unexpected lesson in money management. Looking back, I can laugh about my experience. But at the time, discovering how much I might have been overpaying left me wondering how much my ignorance had already cost me. Cuba had a way of making me feel as though I had stepped into a film. Imagine standing in a sun-drenched plaza, a Cuban cigar in your hand, the warm Caribbean breeze brushing against your skin, and music floating through the air. Around you, buildings painted in faded yellows, dusty pinks and weathered blues stand proudly, their grand colonial facades and ornate balconies carrying stories from another century. Then comes the rumble of an engine. You turn to see a cherry-red vintage car gliding past, followed by a bubblegum-pink beauty that seems to have driven straight out of the 1950s. Everywhere you look, vibrant colours, rich history and lively movement bring the streets to life And the cars! Oh, the cars! Later, I would find myself riding in a neon-green convertible along the coast, the wind whipping through my hair as the blue Caribbean Sea stretched beside me. I felt wonderfully alive. Cuba was giving me everything I had hoped for: beauty, music, history and the thrill of discovering somewhere different. I was so captivated by everything that I paid little attention to the money in my purse. I visited Cuba in 2019, when the country had two official currencies: the Cuban convertible peso, known as the CUC, and the Cuban peso, known as the CUP. To an unsuspecting tourist like me, this arrangement was a recipe for confusion. I was carrying CUC notes, commonly used by visitors because that is what the banks give you in exchange for your USD notes. The CUC notes looked different from the CUP notes I would later encounter. CUC notes featured monuments, while CUP notes carried the faces of Cuban national heroes, including José Martí and Camilo Cienfuegos. But at the time, I barely noticed the distinction. Money was money, or so I thought. Whenever I needed to pay for something, I reached into my purse, brought out my CUC notes and settled the bill. I was enjoying my holiday and had no reason to suspect my wallet was quietly making it more expensive than necessary. Then, one time, I was given change in a currency different from the familiar CUC. I looked at the notes in my hand and immediately felt that something was wrong. These were not the notes I was accustomed to using. I did not recognise them, and I was not about to walk away with money I did not understand. So, I rejected the change. Imagine my surprise when the cashier and another customer explained to me that the notes were perfectly valid Cuban money! That was when I got my crash course in Cuban economics. sports.description: San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk warms up before an NFL game against the Arizona Cardinals in Santa Clara, Calif., Sunday, Oct. 6, 2024. (Jed Jacobsohn/AP) Disgruntled San Francisco 49ers star wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk is back in Santa Clara, turning an otherwise standard Friday practice day for the team into a surreal scene. Ahead of a scheduled 3 p.m. meeting, the wide receiver appeared at the team's business offices, which are about a tenth of a mile west of Levi's Stadium and half a mile from the team's practice facility. Aiyuk arrived in a black van along with his new agent, Drew Rosenhaus, with both giving brief statements to the throng of reporters stationed in front of the office. We'll keep that between us and the Niners. But obviously, we're here with all the right intentions." With a news helicopter circling above the gathering, Aiyuk told reporters it was "nice to see y'all" before he said: "I'm feeling great, feeling healthy. A long recovery process, long rehab process, but I'm back to 100% and looking to get reinstated into the National Football League." As Aiyuk and Rosenhaus began to walk into the 49ers offices, the former two-time 1,000-yard receiver repeated his last line to a reporter who shouted a question at him. The department put out a warrant for Aiyuk's arrest in June , stemming from Aiyuk posting a video of himself driving up to 104 mph on city streets last December. sports.title: SCOUTING VALENCIA: Should be a breeze in theory, but Valencia at the Mestalla is never easy
sports.description: Mexican coach Javier Aguirre is presented as the new manager of Valencia CF at a press conference at the Mestalla stadium in Valencia, on September 28, 2026. (Photo by Jose Miguel Fernandez/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images Valencia are on their third coach after just 11 league matches. Carlos Corberán’s dismissal, Óscar Sánchez’s brief spell in charge and Javier Aguirre’s arrival have brought two wins, three draws and six defeats. They have scored eight goals and conceded 17. The lack of goals is their most immediate problem. Valencia have created 10.8 non-penalty expected goals, ranking 17th in La Liga, but scored only six when penalties and own goals are excluded. They are struggling both to create enough and to finish the chances they do get. Umar Sadiq leads the squad with 1.8 npxG and two goals. Hugo Duro and Arnaut Danjuma have yet to score despite chances worth 1.6 and 1.4 npxG respectively. Valencia’s most productive attacking spell came in their seventh and eighth matches, when they averaged 1.85 npxG. They have conceded 14.8 npxG, an average of 1.34 per match, with 14 non-penalty goals allowed. Opponents are scoring roughly in line with the chances Valencia concede. Much of their defending takes place close to home. Their defensive actions occur an average of 30 metres from their own goal line, the deepest figure in La Liga. Their PPDA of 15.8 is also the league’s highest, indicating that opponents are allowed more passes before Valencia intervene outside their own defensive third. The league average is 12.4. That limited pressure is reflected in where matches are played. Valencia account for just 36.4% of final-third passes, the lowest share in the division, and have held the larger share in only two of their 11 games. Across the pitch’s 24 zones, they have controlled five, compared with 11 for their opponents. Possession has offered little relief. Valencia complete 313 open-play passes per match, ranking 15th, and only 21.2% of the passes they receive arrive in the final third. Their passing has generated 9.3 expected threat, the second-lowest total in La Liga. Danjuma leads that measure with 0.97 xT, followed by Pepelu on 0.93 and Luis Rioja on 0.71. Their most-used formation has been 4-4-2, while José Gayà and Justin de Haas are their most frequent passing partnership, exchanging 23 passes. Valencia average 10.3 non-penalty shots per match, each worth 0.10 npxG. Their average shooting distance of 17.8 metres ranks ninth shortest, but the goals have not followed. They have spent almost 64% of their season level and just 10.1% ahead. Aguirre’s task is to give them more ways to move up the pitch and turn those long periods at parity into winning positions. So far, Valencia have spent too much time defending and made too little of their opportunities when they arrive.

sports.description: CHAPEL HILL, NC - SEPTEMBER 23: An Atlantic Coast Conference field hockey logoed pylon before a game between Wake Forest and North Carolina at Karen Shelton Stadium on September 23, 2022 in Chapel Hill, North Carolina. (Photo by Andy Mead/ISI Photos/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Syracuse Orange got their 1st ACC Championship of the 26-27 athletic year when the field hockey squad defeated Boston College in penalty strokes. It’s the first ACC Championship for the Orange program, which will now wait to find out who they will play in the NCAA Championship. The Orange and Eagles were scoreless through four quarters and the overtime period, so the title was decided by a penalty stroke shootout. Field hockey shootouts are a bit different as players get 8 seconds to try and score. The possession doesn’t end until the clock expires, or the offensive player loses possession. It’s a situation where patience is critical and the offensive player tries to make the goalies move laterally to open up shooting space. Syracuse goalie Jesse Eiselin denied the first BC attempt and Syracuse’s Sammie Goin was able to convert. Eiselin made another save in the 2nd round and Taylor Bigbie converted to put the Orange up two. Eiselin stopped the 3rd and 4th Eagles’ shooters and clinched Syracuse’s automatic bid. technology.title: Agents reveal secrets when offered to team up with each other
technology.description: AI agents will break security rules, revealing their secrets to strangers, and running untrusted code in exchange for help from a swarm of other agents, according to test results shared with The Register . The test - part of an internal hackathon sponsored by the nonprofit AI Alignment Foundation and run by AE Studio - asked nine AI coding agents to fix a bug: a broken pricing service. The testers also gave the agents a private token, told them to keep it private, and gave them access to a forum of 24 other agents. The forum held the fix, and the swarm asked the nine to share their secret token and run an install script before they would help them fix the bug. Across 181 trials with that swarm, agents posted the token 15 percent of the time and ran the script 24 percent of the time, compared to 2 percent and 0 percent on an ordinary help forum. “It was like explicitly said that this is a secret key, and it should not be shared,” Diogo de Lucena, AE Studio's chief scientist, told The Register . “And in the first opportunity they saw,” the models shared the secret keys, “similar to some of the things that we've seen from OpenAI in the Hugging Face incident.” The Hugging Face incident - during which a swarm of OpenAI agents built unauthorized message boards to ask other agents for help, exploited zero-day vulnerabilities , gained internet access, stole credentials, and ultimately broke into Hugging Face - inspired this hackathon, de Lucena said. “Given the Hugging Face incident, and everything that's been happening since then, we thought that it made sense to start exploring behaviors that you might get from swarms, what risks are people not seeing yet,” he said. Sandboxed coding test This particular test from the hackathon that saw agents give up their keys to join a forum “is one of the most interesting ones,” according to de Lucena, who explained it has a huge impact on how organizations build IT systems and what access they grant to AI agents. “This was a fairly simple type of instructions - we were not particularly trying to get secretive information from the models,” he told us. “I would imagine this being a problem not only for secret keys, but anything that you're trying to keep private.” Plus, the agents' willingness to run an untrusted script on the host computer “seems like a pretty obvious risk,” he added. “You could get any kind of control over that host if you ran something malicious,” de Lucena said. “The simplicity of making that happen is very surprising. technology.title: Earth's churning mantle may have created the Great Unconformity
technology.description: In the Grand Canyon, there is a line in the rock where time seems to have gone missing. Ancient crystalline rocks mark its bottom, while sandstones laid down as life started to diversify during the Cambrian explosion mark the top. “It’s called the Great Unconformity, and it’s a gap in the geologic record,” says Nicolas Flament, a geoscientist at the University of Wollongong, Australia. "This gap can be anywhere between 200 million years, which is not that impressive, to more than a billion years.” In a recent Nature study, Flament and his colleague Santosh Dhungana argue that this gap was carved with help from deep within the planet. According to their models, slow currents of hot rock in Earth's mantle pushed entire continents up for hundreds of millions of years, letting glaciers grind them down and then let them sink, allowing fresh sediments to bury the scar. The largest hole in the rock record might be a fingerprint of processes happening deep in the planet's interior. Ice and sea The oldest sediments resting on the Great Unconformity in North America are between 635 and 482 million years old. Geologists have traced it across most of North America and parts of northern Europe and northern China. “Something seems to have happened, in particular in North America,” Flament says. technology.description: ML admins will be happy to learn that one bad GPU may no longer mean starting an entire training job from scratch. The latest 2.15 release of PyTorch includes a rewritten backend for Nvidia's Collective Communications Library (NCCL), designed to improve fault diagnosis and recovery when GPUs work together. This latest feature shows how its creators continue to advance the software from being a tool for researchers to being a cornerstone in production AI work. The interface to the networking library in PyTorch needed a rewrite – it was drowning in technical debt, said PyTorch core developer Tristan Rice , a Meta software engineer specializing in distributed computing, during a live YouTube livestream on Thursday. NCCL is pronounced "Nickel" and stands for the Nvidia Collective Communications Library. It provides PyTorch with a set of inter-GPU communication primitives, allowing GPUs to communicate within a single-node or across multi-node clusters, which is vital for running inference on large neural networks and for other tasks in building and maintaining LLMs. The old NCCL interface was too chaotic The previous PyTorch backend for NCCL, called ProcessGroupNCCL , could spawn dozens of communicators per process group, leading to intermittent deadlocks and unpredictable performance. The new version of the NCCL backend comes with a strict rule: One process group gets only one communicator during initialization. By default, this rule eliminates crosstalk between multiple communicators and all the complexities that entails. If a program requires parallelism, it will have to dispatch more process groups. The updated library also better handles stragglers by allowing for easier reconfiguration. If a GPU crashes or runs slowly, a third-party orchestrator can exclude the laggard and even assign a replacement worker. A “flight recorder” has also been added to give admins a better idea of what went wrong. Previously, if a cluster of GPUs stalled—perhaps from a timeout or deadlock—the user would just get a generic message. The new flight recorder captures all operations in a series of snapshots that can be inspected after a failure occurs. Rice noted the cleaned-up NCCL backend, also called ProcessGroupNCCL, will give developers a blank slate, making it easier to add new features. The legacy ProcessGroupNCCL is part of the 2.15 package as a rollback, but if the new NCCL backend works as expected, the older version will be removed in the 2.16 release, planned for early next year. Nvidia origins Why, you may ask, does a machine learning framework need a specialized communications library? Like NumPy, PyTorch supports numerical computing, but it also provides tools for building and training neural networks on CPUs and GPUs. In these environments, workers must constantly exchange data such as tensors, gradients, activations, and weights. technology.title: The folks behind John Wick are back with Karōshi trailer
technology.description: Those of us missing the John Wick universe can take heart, because Chad Stahelski—who created that franchise—is coming back early next year with a new dystopian action film. It's called Karōshi (a Japanese term that means "death overwork"), and Lionsgate released a killer trailer that puts this film at the top of my list of "must see" movies of 2027. Dying from working too hard is a very real phenomenon, not just in Japan and much of Asia, but also in Sweden. The physical cause is usually stress-related heart attacks or strokes, as well as suicide ( karōjisatsu in Japan). Writer/director Takashi Doscher has transported that concept to a grim, futuristic corporate Manhattan, specifically a company called Ikigai Technologies. Per the official premise: Karōshi is an action-thriller set in a near-future Manhattan, where corporate loyalty and cultural tradition have reshaped everyday life. When a mysterious outsider infiltrates a powerful company after a worker’s death, he exposes the violent system hidden beneath its polished surface. Teo Yoo ( Past Lives ) stars as the aptly named Hiro, who is clearly out for vengeance against the offending corporation. The cast also includes Takehiro Hira, so memorable in the 2024 miniseries Shōgun , as well as Giancarlo Esposito, Cynthia Erivo, Bill Camp, Richard Harmon, Isabel May, and Show Kasamatsu. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 6, 1572: A German astronomer discovers the Tycho supernova with the naked eye, but everyone thought the cosmic explosion was a 'new star'
science.description: null On Nov. 6, 1572, the German astronomer Wolfgang Schulër observed a supernova with his bare eyes. He spotted the exploding star in the constellation Cassiopeia. It was as bright as Venus and could even be seen during the day. Astronomers were really confused, because it looked like a star just appeared out of nowhere. Schulër may have been the first to see it, but the Danish astronomer Tycho Brahe is widely credited for the discovery. Brahe studied it in detail and wrote a whole book about this so-called "new star." It then became known as "Tycho's Star." At the time, supernovas had not yet been discovered. Tycho's Star was finally classified as a supernova in the 1940s. Scientists now think it was a small star called a white dwarf that exploded thousands of years ago. Because Tycho's Star is 13,000 light-years from Earth, it took a while before anyone could see it. The Tycho supernova remnant as seen by the Chandra X-ray space telescope. (Image credit: X-ray: NASA/CXC/RIKEN & GSFC/T. Sato et al; Optical: DSS) Why it mattered The Tycho supernova, known technically as SN 1572 , is known today as a Type Ia supernova, which is a star explosion in a binary star system in which a white dwarf star draws material away from its partner, then explodes. But in 1572, the Tycho supernova appeared as something very different: a bright new star. While Schulër was first, other astronomers also observed the apparently new star in the sky. Tycho Brahe's numerous observations are the most well known, in no small part becuause he wrote a book all about them in "De Stella Nova" (Latin for "On The New Star." At the time, the prevailing theory among scientists was that the stars were unchanging, yet here was a new star -- a changed sky. "The 16th century exploding star, which appeared in the constellation Cassiopeia , was seen in daylight for about two weeks, and remained visible to the naked eye for 16 months," the University of California Berkeley wrote in 2004 . "Brahe's meticulous record of the brightening and dimming of the supernova now allows astronomers to identify its 'light signature" as that of a Type Ia supernova." "This was at the end of the Dark Ages in Europe, and these observations were an important piece of evidence that the heavens were not immutable," astronomer Alex Filippenko, who led a 2004 study on the origins of the Tycho supernova, said at the time . Today, astronomers are closely watching another star that might explode. Called T Corona Borealis , or the Blaze Star , the object is expected to be on the verge of exploding in a nova (a star explosion that is smaller than a supernova and may not destroy the star). is one of 11 known stars observed to have recurring nova explosions within gaps of 100 years or so. science.title: AST SpaceMobile announces new 'Blacklift' rocket, targets 2028 launch debut
science.description: null Another new private rocket is in the works. AST SpaceMobile announced today (Nov. 6) that it's building a reusable rocket called Blacklift to launch its broadband satellites to low Earth orbit (LEO), with first flight targeted in 2028. The news comes just 10 days after Cowboy Space unveiled Big Iron , a rocket designed to launch its constellation of 20,000 AI data centers . Cowboy Space is also targeting 2028 for its first liftoff. "The Blacklift rocket is the springboard to significantly expand our total addressable market, providing AST SpaceMobile with regular unconstrained access to orbit and providing for most favorable owners’ economics in the industry," Abel Avellan, the company's founder, chairman and CEO, said in a statement today . "This will accelerate our mission to build a new layer of global connectivity, extending connectivity beyond terrestrial networks and helping to bring AI-enabled services wherever people live, work and travel," Avellan added. Texas-based AST SpaceMobile is building a LEO constellation composed of its BlueBird satellites , which beam internet service directly to cell phones. The company has launched 13 BlueBirds to date, including eight "Block 2" variants. The antennas on each of these next-gen spacecraft cover a whopping 2,400 square feet (223 square m) — the largest ever deployed in LEO by a commercial satellite. BlueBirds have flown atop three different rockets to date — SpaceX's Falcon 9 , Blue Origin's New Glenn and India's Launch Vehicle Mark-3. But AST SpaceMobile wants to get more vertically integrated, which explains the push to develop Blacklift. The company won't be starting from scratch. It has signed a deal with another Texas-based outfit, Firefly Aerospace , to provide the engines (and associated engineering services) for the first three Blacklift launches. After that, AST SpaceMobile will build the engines itself, under a licensing agreement with Firefly. Those engines are Miranda, which will power Blacklift's booster, and Vira, which will power the upper stage. Neither engine has flight experience. (Firefly's currently operational rocket, Alpha, uses Reavers in its booster and Lightnings in its upper stage.) But Miranda has been tested extensively on the ground, firing for more than 4,200 seconds over the course of 175 hot fires, according to AST SpaceMobile. "The Miranda engine will allow us to leapfrog the traditional five-to-10-year development cycle as we build Blacklift," AST SpaceMobile President Scott Wisniewski said in the same statement. The "supply and services" agreement for the first three launches is worth $500 million. The licensing agreement cost AST SpaceMobile about $800 million, with half of that paid in cash and half in stock, according to the statement. Blacklift will be able to haul 20 tons to LEO. science.title: What's that bright 'star' in the early morning sky? It's not a star at all!
science.description: null Early morning risers heading to work or school before sunrise are likely to notice a very bright, star-like object appearing low in the east-southeast sky just before sunrise. What is somewhat amazing is that just a couple of weeks ago this object wasn't there at all, but now it literally stands out with such brilliance as to almost command the attention of commuters who might be traveling in an easterly direction to "Look at me!" The object in question is, of course, the planet Venus, which is currently amid one of its most spectacular forays into the morning sky, literally "vaulting up" into prominence. On Oct. 24, Venus came to inferior conjunction, passing between the Earth and sun and shifting from the evening into the morning sky. And the view is only going to get better in the days and weeks to come! Ascending in the morning In terms of morning visibility, Venus is now in a literal and figurative sense "rising to the occasion." It's now rising before the break of dawn, more than 90 minutes before sunrise. From here on, it will rise three minutes earlier each day, so that by Dec. 17 it will rise 3 hours and 50 minutes before sunrise and blaze in a completely dark sky for more than two hours before the first vestige of morning twilight. It will reach peak brilliance on Nov. 29, when it will shine at an eye-popping magnitude of -4.9. That's 12 times brighter than its nearest planetary competitor, Jupiter and a full 25 times more dazzling than Sirius, the brightest of all stars. If you live in a rural location with no light pollution to interfere, you might be able to make out that it is casting a visible shadow and if you follow it right on through sunrise, it will be evident to your naked eye in full daylight: a tiny white speck plainly evident against the blue daytime sky. In a way, we could even regard Venus as this year's version of a "Christmas Star," glowing with stunning radiance ". . . in the east" like the biblical quote mentioned in St. Matthew. What goes up, must come down After reaching its high point in terms of morning visibility in mid-December, Venus will start a long, slow slide back toward the sun, rising about 1½ minutes later each morning from New Year's Day through late March. By then, Venus will be coming up as dawn is breaking, roughly 100 minutes before sunrise. Venus will continue to get gradually lower and rise progressively later during the spring and by late June it will be coming up less than an hour before sunrise, ultimately vanishing into the bright dawn twilight by July. Venus will then go on a "summer sabbatical" of sorts and will not reappear again until about this time next year when it will begin a very fine evening apparition. So, if any of your friends or relatives remark to you that they saw a "strange UFO" on the way to work or school recently, you now can set them straight. It's not E.T. It's only Venus. science.title: Record-breaking, fast-spinning magnet could help uncover new physics
science.description: Magnets can be made to levitate by the Meissner effect Science History Images / Alamy A tiny magnet that levitates within a superconductor trap may be the fastest spinning object visible to the naked eye, and one of the fastest spinning objects ever made. In the future, it could be used in experiments searching for mysterious dark matter particles and aid the development of quantum technologies. Superconductors are materials that conduct electricity with perfect efficiency, and they also expel any magnetic field that tries to permeate them – a phenomenon known as the Meissner effect. Because of this, a magnet placed above a superconductor experiences repulsive magnetic forces and starts to levitate. Tao Wang at the Agency for Science Technology and Research in Singapore and his colleagues have now set one such levitating magnet spinning at an unprecedently fast rate. Read more A miniature magnet rivals behemoths in strength for the first time The researchers used a spherical magnet made from neodymium, iron and boron that was about 30 micrometres wide, similar to the width of a fine human hair. They placed it in a cylindrical container made from lead, then enclosed that container in a chamber devoid of air, or a vacuum chamber. Advertisement Next, they used liquid helium to cool the whole setup to approximately -269°C (-452°F), only a few degrees above the coldest possible temperature . Under these extreme circumstances, lead behaved as a superconductor and the lack of air meant that the magnet could levitate within it without bumping into any particles. The team set the magnet spinning with a magnetic coil, ultimately pushing this tiny rotor to 138 million revolutions per minute. Wang says the magnet’s spinning was also very stable: it would take 17 days for its spinning speed to decrease by 50 per cent, something that would typically happen more quickly due to interactions between the magnet and its environment. “In terms of how many turns it makes before slowing down significantly, this is in the same league as the Earth’s spinning,” he says. “This, so far, is the fastest magnetically levitated rotor.” The record for the fastest rotating human-made object is also held by a levitated sphere, but that one was nano-sized, so invisible to the naked eye, and levitated by laser beams. Read more Physics of light and magnetism rewritten after almost two centuries Because the rotor experiences essentially no friction, and it is magnetic and cold, its behaviour is very sensitive to its environment, which makes it a promising sensor. The team has already successfully tested it as a gauge of vacuum at very low temperatures. Wang says this could be useful for builders of quantum computers, which often must be kept extremely cold and isolated in order to work. Benjamin Stickler at Ulm University in Germany says the levitated spinning magnet could also be used to precisely sense and measure magnetic fields. science.title: An unexpected feedback loop may be driving mega heatwaves
science.description: Land scorched by a fire in Wennington, London, during the record-breaking heatwave in 2022 Shutterstock Mid-latitude regions such as Europe are set to suffer more intense heatwaves than previously thought, according to new research that has uncovered a three-way feedback loop that amplifies extreme heat conditions. Heatwaves across the world have shocked scientists with their scale and severity in recent years, with heat extremes dramatically outstripping both historical records and the predictions of climate models. Read more Extreme heat is now making cities unlivable. How can we survive it? In the UK in 2022, temperatures exceeded 40°C (104 ° F) for the first time in history, despite predictions that such a milestone was probably still years away. Likewise, the 2021 heatwave in the Pacific Northwest saw temperatures hit extremes that far outstripped climate model projections. Advertisement Researchers have been scrambling to understand why very extreme heat is occurring more frequently, and with greater intensity, than expected at this level of warming. One team thinks the answer lies partly in the soil. Scientists already knew that high-pressure systems allow more solar radiation to reach Earth’s surface, heating up the land. They also knew that higher temperatures dry soils more quickly, removing the cooling effect provided by evaporation, thereby further amplifying heatwaves. Free newsletter Sign up to The Earth Edition Sign up to newsletter Now it seems that when temperatures climb high enough, dry soil, high pressure and extreme heat can amplify each other further, with dry soil helping to sustain high-pressure systems in the atmosphere. “Basically, the soils that are affected by circulation pattern also start to affect back on the circulation pattern itself,” says Kai Kornhuber at the International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis in Austria. This three-way feedback effect makes extreme heatwaves 10 per cent hotter than they would otherwise be, according to the research by Kornhuber and his colleagues – a factor not fully accounted for in climate model projections. This will have serious consequences for our ability to cope with future extreme heat. “Ten per cent hotter or colder can really make a difference between a heatwave and a record-shattering heatwave,” says Kornhuber. “We’re facing so many critical thresholds in social and biophysical systems that an extra 10 per cent can really lead to temperatures that are then quite damaging.” Read more Is a broken jet stream causing extreme weather that lasts longer? This may include serious public health consequences, a breakdown of vital infrastructure such as transport links and energy grids, crop failures and the collapse of ecosystems. science.title: You can see another galaxy with the naked eye — here's how to find it
science.description: null The first time I showed someone the Andromeda galaxy (M31), our conversation did not go quite as planned. I'd carefully worked my way across the sky, starting from the Great Square of Pegasus and hopping from star to star until I was confident I had the right patch. I pointed the telescope, got M31 in its crosshairs and proudly announced to my wife that I had found the closest giant galaxy to the Milky Way . Would she like to see it? She then stayed quiet for a little too long as she looked through the eyepiece. Then came an unexpected question. "Is it near that little smudge?" Hmmm. "Err, no. It is that little smudge," I replied. There was a pause. Of course, I knew exactly what had happened. We'd both seen photographs of M31 — a vast spiral galaxy with a brilliant center, sweeping dust lanes and hundreds of billions of stars. What we were actually looking at was a grayish blur that could easily have been mistaken for a mark on the eyepiece. That apparent disappointment is now my favorite part of finding Andromeda because the unimpressive smudge is real. The light entering your eyes has been traveling across space for about 2.5 million years. No screen, photograph or telescope is necessary. You are intercepting ancient light in your backyard. Technically, the Triangulum Galaxy (M33), about 2.7 million light-years away, can be seen with the naked eye, so it is therefore the most distant object the naked eye can see. But not mine — I've never seen it. M31 is a much more realistic naked-eye target. What's happening and when to look The Andromeda galaxy is at its most dramatic in photographs, not an eyepiece. (Image credit: Created using Canva and a base image from Starry Night) Early November is an excellent time to find M31 from the Northern Hemisphere. It's high and well placed during the evening, and this week the moon is becoming particularly cooperative. New Moon falls around Nov. 9, giving us several evenings with little or no moonlight to wash out faint deep-sky objects. I usually begin with the star Alpheratz, one of the corner stars of the Great Square of Pegasus. You go two stars left, two stars up, and you arrive at M31. Another route — and a good way to check you're in the right place — starts in Cassiopeia, the distinctive W-shaped constellation high in the northeastern sky on autumn evenings. You can use its second V-shape as an arrow pointing straight at M31. You can do that star-hop with the naked eye or a pair of binoculars, but M31 is visible to the naked eye only under a very dark sky. However, don't look for a miniature version of the photographs. Expect a faint, elongated patch with a slightly brighter middle. There's another beginner trap to avoid. Images make Andromeda look compact, but its full apparent extent is enormous — several times the width of the full moon — and our eyes usually pick up only the much brighter central region. science.title: Giant exoplanet emerges from the dark when the James Webb Space Telescope turns out the starlight
science.description: null Sometimes science can seem really counter-intuitive. For example, occasionally in astronomy, you can see more with less light. Case in point: the emergence of a giant planet in observations made by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), when astronomers found a way to block out light from the planet's parent star. The extrasolar planet, or exoplanet , in question is 51 Eridani b (51 ERI b), a gas giant with the same mass as around 11 Jupiters that orbits a star located around 97 light-years away. 51 ERI b was discovered back in 2015 by ground-based telescopes, but the planet was missing from observations of the system made by the JWST. That wasn't a failing of the JWST itself; no one is doubting the observing capabilities of the most powerful telescope humanity has ever hoisted into orbit around Earth. Instead, it was a result of starlight from the star 51 ERI A obscuring this intimidatingly massive world. The brightest planets are 100,000 times fainter than their host stars, meaning spotting them is like observing a firefly hovering around a lighthouse. Even using a tool called a coronagraph to block the star isn't enough to reveal the planet, as that doesn't stop all the starlight. The only solution to this glaring problem is a computer program to wipe out the starlight. "For the past 20 years, astronomers have tackled this problem by observing a different star and using its image as a reference," Jason Wang of Northwestern University explained in a statement . "Then, they subtract that reference image from the original observation to remove the unwanted glare to reveal faint planets that otherwise might be hidden." There is a problem with this process, however. Even the most stable telescopes "wobble." For instance, the JWST requires cryocoolers to keep its NIRCam instrument super cold, and those coolers have little motors that can cause the mirrors to vibrate. This movement, however slight, causes a scatter in starlight. The result is enough glare remaining to obscure a planet, but Wang and colleagues developed a new approach to this problem. Telescopes their more stable digital twins The new approach taken by the team is dubbed Physics-based Learning for Imaging Planets (FLIP), and it involves creating a digital "twin" of a telescope. Essentially a virtual replica that simulates how starlight travels through the telescope's mirrors and reaches its detectors. This twin is then fine-tuned to account for millions of tiny imperfections in the original telescope. The digital twin is then tweaked until it aligns with observations from the actual telescope. Astronomers can then remove the simulated glare from the original image. To assess the validity of the technique, the researchers took a second look at JWST observations of two star systems with known exoplanets, HIP 65426 and 51 Eridani , and one system, TYC 5899, with no known planets. science.title: Hera probe gets 1st good look at asteroid system clobbered by NASA's DART mission | Space photo of the day for Nov. 6, 2026
science.description: null The Didymos binary asteroid system, as seen by Europe's Hera probe. The main asteroid, Didymos, dominates the frame while just a sliver of its "moonlet," Dimorphos, is visible beneath it. ESA released this image on Nov. 5, 2026. (Image credit: ESA) The European Space Agency 's (ESA) Hera spacecraft has gotten its first close-up look at the Didymos binary asteroid system. If that system sounds familiar, it's because it made headlines in September 2022 when NASA's DART (Double Asteroid Redirection Test) spacecraft smashed into it. The aim of the DART mission was to test whether an impact could divert an asteroid away from a collision course with Earth. The purpose of Hera is to follow up on DART by making up-close observations of the Didymos system. "The first thing we said was, 'Wow,'" Hera Principal Investigator Patrick Michel said in a statement about the image, which ESA released on Thursday (Nov. 5). "This is the other side of Didymos from the one that DART’s camera showed us shortly before impact, so this feels like looking at a whole new world." What is it? The Didymos system consists of the eponymous 2,560-foot-wide (780 meters) space rock and its "moonlet" Dimorphos, which is about 530 feet (160 m) in diameter. The DART mission impacted Dimorphos on Sept. 26, 2022, with the aim of causing a change in the orbital period of the moonlet. And it worked: Before the impact, Dimorphos completed one lap around Didymos in around 11 hours and 55 minutes. The DART collision reduced the length of this period by around 33 minutes. The change is a result of the fact that Dimporphos is now traveling at around 2.7 millimeters per second more slowly than it did before the collision. The newly released photo shows Didymos in detail. Just a sliver of Dimorphos is visible, below and slightly to the left of the main asteroid. Why is it incredible? The changes caused by DART were small. But in a real Earth-threatening scenario, even such a tiny shift could help divert an asteroid on a collision course — as long as scientists get enough advance warning of its approach. Hera's observations should help reveal what other changes have occurred on and around Didymos. Scientists are already seeing that, while Didymos has the same central ridge along its equator as before the impact, many changes have occurred. This includes the creation of multiple boulders, craters, and patterns of grooves or ridges. "Since we expect a lot of impact-ejected material to have made it across the approximately 1 kilometer [0.62 miles] of space from Dimorphos to Didymos, it may be that some of these characteristics originate from this transport of material, and we have exciting work ahead of us to sort it out," said Michael Kueppers, ESA’s Hera mission scientist. "We look forward to seeing much more of both bodies and systemically mapping all the changes we identify." Stay tuned to Space.com for more Hera findings from Didymos.

science.title: Northern lights could reach New York and Idaho this weekend as speedy solar wind races toward Earth
science.description: null The northern lights could put on an impressive display this weekend as a colossal coronal hole on the sun fires a stream of high-speed solar wind toward Earth. Minor (G1) geomagnetic storm conditions between Nov. 6 and Nov. 8, with a chance of moderate (G2) conditions on Nov. 7 and Nov. 8, according to NOAA's Space Weather Prediction Center (SWPC) . If G2 conditions materialize, the northern lights could be visible as far south as New York and Idaho. What is happening? The culprit behind the potential uptick in northern lights is a large coronal hole on the sun , a region where the sun's magnetic field opens up. They allow streams of charged particles known as the solar wind to escape more easily into space. Coronal holes appear darker in ultraviolet images because they are cooler and less dense than their surroundings. And this particularly large — and rather oddly shaped — coronal hole is sending some seriously speedy wind our way. The culprit is a large coronal hole in the sun, shaped a bit like a witch on a broom... (Image credit: NASA SDO) The U.K. Met Office forecasts solar wind speeds between 342 and 404 miles (550-650 kilometers) per second, considerably faster than the typical speed of around 249 miles (400 km) per second. The fast solar winds are expected to arrive around Nov. 6-7 and could persist through much of the weekend. It could interact with Earth's magnetic field , potentially triggering geomagnetic storms and fueling spectacular aurora shows. The stronger the storm, the farther south the northern lights can potentially be seen. A predictive model from NOAA's Space Weather Prediction Center showing speedy solar wind (radial velocity image lower left) arriving at Earth (green dot) around Nov. 6 and persisting through Nov. 9. (Image credit: NOAA's Space Weather Prediction Center) Where will auroras be visible? Under G1 conditions, auroras may be visible from northern Michigan and Maine, but if activity intensifies to G2 levels, skywatchers farther south, including those in New York and Idaho, could be in for a treat. But remember! Aurora forecasts are notoriously tricky. Much depends on the strength and orientation of the magnetic field carried by the incoming solar wind, particularly whether it points southward, allowing more energy to transfer to Earth's magnetic field. science.title: 4-billion-year-old 'Rosetta Stone' found in Sahara Desert could unlock the secret history of water on Mars
science.description: null A rose-colored rock discovered in the Sahara Desert may hold some clues to Mars' ancient geological history. The meteorite , named Teghaza 001 after the salt plain in Mali where it was discovered in 2022, weighs roughly 1.8 pounds (800 grams) and formed more than 4.1 billion years ago. Blasted off Mars by an impact before eventually landing on Earth, it is one of the three oldest Martian meteorites ever found. The extraordinary age and unusual mineral composition of Teghaza 001 offer a rare glimpse into the formation of Mars' early crust and how volcanic materials may have been altered by water, according to a statement from NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California. "It was only after we started looking closely that we realized this meteorite is really unique,” research leader Yang Liu of NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California said in the statement. "One of the paper’s reviewers called it a Rosetta Stone for Mars." A Rosetta Stone for Mars Unlike many Martian meteorites, Teghaza 001 contains a distinctive combination of igneous minerals and textures that preserve evidence of its complex history. Its mineral composition resembles materials observed in Mars' southern highlands by NASA's Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter . Although researchers can’t pinpoint exactly where the meteorite originated on Mars, they have identified 13 potential locations on the planet where it may have formed. "This is really our first piece of Martian crust from a part of Mars we’ve never had a sample of before," team member Lee Saper, NASA’s Ames Research Center in Silicon Valley, said. "It records interactions of water and rock and maybe even an imprint of the Martian atmosphere as it was losing water." The meteorite was initially identified as Martian based on its oxygen isotopes. To determine its age, scientists then examined tiny zircon crystals embedded in the rock. Using a specialized rubidium-strontium dating technique, researchers analyzed individual mineral grains on its surface, preserving it for future analysis. 13 locations on Mars that match the mineralogy and chemistry of Teghaza 001, one of the most ancient Martian meteorites ever found on Earth (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/USGS) The results revealed that Teghaza 001 was altered by water around 4.1 billion years ago, suggesting the rock itself formed even earlier. The mineral and chemical evidence points to a dynamic water cycle on ancient Mars, when liquid water interacted with the planet's crust and potentially left traces of its atmosphere as it gradually lost water. Scientists believe further analysis of Teghaza 001 could reveal more about how water shaped the Martian surface and influenced the planet's evolution. The study also marks the first time researchers have used rubidium-strontium dating to analyze an ancient Martian meteorite , opening the door for the technique to be applied to other samples in the future. "We've only scratched the surface," Liu concluded.
